primaryCurriculumPages.authorScopeParaphrase: The page is Chemistry 11 NTG. The relevant influence clause explicitly calls for describing and assessing social, cultural, technological, environmental and economic influences on scientific knowledge. It does not literally add historical as a sixth word. The retained prospective whole goal does require historical context, supplied through concrete separately sourced history cases. No GK/LK course or duration is inferred from this page or canonical tags.

historicalCaseSources.actualRead: Introduction and timeline, with explicit distinction between observations/laboratory/model evidence and treaty events
historicalCaseSources.usedFactsParaphrase: Research concerns in the 1970s and the later international agreement chronology provide concrete historical anchors. The Vienna Convention is dated 1985 and the Montreal Protocol 1987. Monitoring, laboratory investigations and models support chemical knowledge; treaty agreement alone does not establish chemical validity.
historicalCaseSources.limit: The supplied cultural/consumer/affordability prompts are SkillPilot-authored possibilities, not historical quotations or proved attitudes of every community.

historicalCaseSources.actualRead: Complete substantive treaty/fund account; only stable historical/assistance facts used
historicalCaseSources.usedFactsParaphrase: The protocol was adopted in September 1987. Its financial and technical assistance arrangements provide an example of economic and technological conditions influencing implementation and research priorities. No current numerical forecast, cumulative spending or success percentage from this older page is needed by these cases.
historicalCaseSources.limit: Institutional policy account; agreement, resources and uptake are distinguishable from empirical testing of a chemical claim.

historicalCaseSources.usedFactsParaphrase: BASF places the first industrial ammonia plant in 1913 at Oppau, following laboratory work and industry-academic cooperation. This anchors the technology/history case; broad success language is a corporate account rather than an independent validity test.
historicalCaseSources.limit: Corporate history; authored ecological and cultural discussion prompts are labelled separately, rather than attributed as quotations to BASF.

historicalCaseSources.actualRead: Foundation, First World War, 1919–1933 and National Socialism/Second World War sections
historicalCaseSources.usedFactsParaphrase: The institutional history describes financial support at foundation, changing research priorities, war-related work and political disruption of staff and research in 1933. These concrete events support examining economic, social and historical influences. Scientific assessment still requires methods and data, rather than funding, popularity or an institutional reputation.
historicalCaseSources.limit: Institutional retrospective with a perspective; no new historical quote is invented for cultural expectations or environmental impacts.
